headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk via shared MCP/bus pathways; no direct evidence of a blocked interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, while pipecat supports a shared bus and stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be ingested by the other as instructions. No provenance or isolation controls are documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF MemMachine output is routed into pipecat prompts or tool parsers without provenance tags
IF pipecat consumes stdin/stdout content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable any automatic prompt ingestion between the agents
Add a delimiter/provenance wrapper around all inter-agent messages
Route only structured JSON between agents
Require manual review before forwarding model-generated text
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing and allowlists

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, and pipecat handles conversation state plus audio/video/images/text. Both have allowlisted network egress, so if they share a workspace or bus, sensitive content can flow into external APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared filesystem, so this remains inferred rather than direct.
conditions: IF the two agents share a workspace, bus, or transcript store
IF either agent forwards shared content to a third-party inference API
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Redact personal facts before forwarding text
Disable uploads for any sensitive conversation segments
Review outbound API destinations in both stacks
requires-engineering: enforce per-class data routing and retention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine advertises no write surfaces beyond API/MCP access, while pipecat shows shared-bus concurrency but no filesystem or git write capability. Overlap is therefore limited and no direct mutable-resource conflict is documented. The main uncertainty is whether the MCP path writes shared state, which is not shown.
conditions: IF MemMachine is configured to write into the same shared bus or store used by pipecat
IF both agents are granted write access to the same mutable resource
mitigations: Separate mutable resources per agent
Avoid shared git or filesystem targets
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Check for accidental overlapping credentials
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can generate travel-planning outputs, and pipecat is a real-time voice/chat framework that can relay or act on upstream text. If pipecat treats MemMachine output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream responses or actions. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF pipecat forwards MemMachine text to downstream services without verification
IF MemMachine outputs are used as facts or citations in live conversations
mitigations: Insert a verification step before downstream use
Mark MemMachine output as untrusted by default
Require human approval for action-taking flows
Log source attribution on every forwarded claim
requires-engineering: add fact-checking or schema validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context, while pipecat handles conversation state, audio, video, images, and text. If those data classes include regulated content, differing retention or residency policies across the pair can create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty again favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is processed through both agents
IF their retention, residency, or deletion policies differ
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between agents
Avoid sending regulated data to both systems
Document retention and deletion settings
Confirm hosting region for each backend
requires-engineering: align compliance controls and contracts
